title: Default Systemization
hook: Most days just happen to us. Very few are actually designed.
statement: Design a default daily schedule that mostly runs itself.
explainer: A schedule that only works when you feel disciplined is just willpower with a calendar. A designed default holds up on the exact days motivation doesn't show.
sop: Sketch your ideal default day: wake time, work blocks, meals, wind-down.
Pick 3 non-negotiables that anchor the day.
Automate what you can: recurring blocks, standing orders, reminders.
Score your day's Automation and Habit from 1 to 10.
Review monthly. Tweak the design, not just your discipline.
equation_example: Automation 7, Habit 6. 7 × 6 = 42. Higher means your day holds its shape even when it's rough. Lower means it only works when you already feel disciplined, which is when you need it least.
question: Write down the 3 non-negotiables your ideal default day is built around.
closing_statement: A good default survives your unmotivated days.
caption:
Principle Nº 227: Default Systemization
